function.description: Amend a live cron job IN PLACE — patch its task (old_text -> new_text, the rest kept verbatim), or change its schedule, cap, rig, delivery or pinned skills. Use this instead of cancel + re-schedule, which re-types the task and loses its rules. To run a job sooner, set a new schedule (e.g. a one-shot ISO time a minute ahead).
function.name: cronjob_edit

parameters.description: Amend a live job IN PLACE. Pass only the fields to change.

deliver.description: New delivery sink ('telegram'|'email' to the owner, 'twitter' = a PUBLIC X post), or 'none' to drop it.

job_id.description: The id of the cron job to edit.

new_text.description: Replacement for old_text ('' deletes the passage).

old_text.description: Exact passage of the CURRENT task to replace (copy it from cronjob_show; must occur exactly once). The rest of the task is kept verbatim — never re-type a whole task to change one value.

pause_windows.description: Replace the job's pause windows ([[start, end], ...]); [] clears them.

precheck.description: Replace the job's $0 pre-check (see cronjob_schedule); {} clears it.

read_verb.description: Replace the job's read verb (see cronjob_schedule); {} clears it.

rig.description: New named tool rig, or 'none' to clear it.

schedule.description: New schedule spec; the next run is recomputed from now. This is how you run a job SOONER: set a one-shot ISO time a minute ahead. A one-shot spec makes a recurring job one-shot — set its recurring spec back after that run.

skills.description: Replace the pinned skill ids ([] clears them).

target_token.description: Replace the declared buy target {'chain', 'address'}; {} clears it.

write_verb.description: OWNER TURN ONLY: replace the job's write verb (see cronjob_schedule); {} clears it.
